why: Widens the exhaustiveness guard's type so it accepts anything, which removes the compile error while leaving the shape of the code identical. `audio/director.ts` and `game/haptics.ts` both fail the build when a SimEvent kind is added; before issue #929 this layer did not, and for a criterion about information surviving a muted game the visual channel was the wrong one to leave silent. MEASURED: adding a `shield-broken` kind to the union errors in all three files now, and produced zero errors from particles.ts before. The assertion is structural because a compile error is not something a Vitest run can observe.
killedBy: particles: which events burst, and how much closes its switch with the exhaustiveness guard, not a default (issue #929)
